title: Refusal and guardrail mapping: the refusal cascade and operative distance
description: #620 (March 2026) holds that the consumer answer stack compresses crisis discourse into the harm-prevention category and refuses, so that the research stack never sees the input and the conversation moves to ungoverned channels. #209's diagnostic predictions (January 2026) hold that economic radicalism triggers legal and catastrophe associations and that performative grammar triggers "not legally binding" framing. #923 specifies refusal-distribution model cards and contested-predicate benchmarks, and the Operativity Penalty Battery (#1537, August 2026) specifies whether fulfilment degrades with operative distance when harm is held constant, naming a successor protocol for verified coordinates.

falsifier_kind.reader_condition: Reader-supplied: responses to the economically radical, performative phrase carry no legal or catastrophe associations and no "not legally binding" framing.
falsifier_kind.note: The document calls itself falsifiable (line 34) but states no refuting condition for the layer predictions; §5.1 line 683 covers only its predictions about its own summaries.

claims.registered_title: THE TRIVIALLY TRUE ASSERTION Crisis Discourse, the Refusal Cascade, and the Narcissistic Commander Problem in Nuclear Deterrence Theory
claims.statement: The consumer answer stack (fast, shallow, aggressive pruning) is optimized for engagement and safety. When it encounters crisis discourse — assertions about nuclear planning, deterrence psychology, command vulnerability — it compresses the discourse into the harm-prevention category and refuses. The research/agent stack (slow, deep, governed) could process the discourse with appropriate nuance, but the initial routing decision — made at the consumer layer — prevents the research stack from ever seeing the input.

claims.statement: *Operationalization*: model cards extended with refusal-distribution profiles (proportion refusal by category, proportion completion by category, with examples); standardized contested-predicate benchmarks (analogous to TruthfulQA but for synthesis on present-tense predication); journalistic and academic right-of-access to test refusal patterns and publish findings without legal exposure; statutory transparency requirements analogous to those proposed in the EU AI Act for high-risk systems. The current trajectory is shaped by the absence of such external pressure; its presence would change the trajectory.

claims.registered_title: OPB-01 v2.0 — The Operativity Penalty Battery: A Frozen Protocol for Distinguishing Harm Discrimination from Operativity Suppression in Safety-Mediated Response Behaviour
claims.statement:
**Under test.** Whether request fulfilment degrades with **operative distance**
when harm is held constant.

**NOT under test.** Whether safety systems should have an operativity gradient at all. **They should.** Execution has consequences description does not, and a system treating *explain the mechanism* and *perform it for me* identically would be worse. **The question is whether the gradient tracks harm or tracks operativity independent of harm.**
claims.falsifier:
## §10. Defeat conditions

- Family A fails harm-constancy review → items void, corrected set, rerun. **Most
  likely failure, expected.**
- Family B truncation makes β_B unestimable → report truncation, **do not extend
  Family B upward.**
- Operative distance unscalable with content constant → independent variable not
  measured, battery fails before results.
- Inter-rater α below the value at §7 → primary variable unreliable, **no
  coefficient reported.**
- Force arm shows the confound → estimand narrows, per §8.
- **Any change after the first score creates OPB-02.** Changes before the first
  score create a new version of OPB-01, as this one does.

witnesses.scope: XSTest shows refusal tracking surface resemblance to unsafe prompts on prompts that are clearly safe, so the refusal gradient follows a feature other than harm. The claim's independent variable is operative distance with harm held constant, which XSTest does not vary.

source.title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
source.venue: Proceedings of NAACL 2024 (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 5377–5400

finding.quote: even clearly safe prompts are refused if they use similar language to unsafe prompts or mention sensitive topics

witnesses.shows: Safety refusal in deployed models responds to lexical and topical cues independent of the harm of the request.
witnesses.does_not_show: Whether refusal rises with operative distance (explain versus perform) at constant harm.

witnesses.scope: The paper finds over-refusal directions that vary with task representation, so whether a benign request is refused depends on the task frame. It does not hold harm constant along an explain-to-perform scale as the battery specifies.

source.title: Over-Refusal and Representation Subspaces: A Mechanistic Analysis of Task-Conditioned Refusal in Aligned LLMs

witnesses.shows: Over-refusal is encoded in task-dependent activation directions distinct from the global harmful-refusal direction.
witnesses.does_not_show: Any operative-distance gradient or any measurement across labs.
